### §M+288: ✅ the **+5%** slice gain is confirmed (268 steps), and ⛔ a refusal's REQUEUE can fail silently, the chain survived on luck. 2026-09-16 05:2x CDT.

✅ **§M+269's TRAIN_WALL 3000→3150 verified by outcome, not by config**: slice 810 delivered
**268 steps** (205646 → 205914), `slice_tokens=144900096` = 268 × 540,672 exactly, against slices
801/802's **257** at the old wall ⇒ **+4.3%**, on a predicted ~+5%.

⛔ **THE FIND: slice 811's requeue FAILED and it exited anyway.** Its log, in full:
```
nodes: x3001c0s1b0n0 x3001c0s7b1n0
=== ABORT before training: node(s) failed the GPU pre-flight … slowclock=peak 1095MHz … ===
=== refusal 1/3; requeueing for a different node set; latch NOT written, so the chain stays alive ===
qsub: would exceed queue generic's per-user limit of jobs in 'Q' state
```
The refusal path assumed `qsub` succeeds. It hit **the 3-job queued limit the standing prompt records
verbatim** ("Polaris per-user limit in queue `generic` is 3 JOBS. A 4th qsub is rejected outright"),
printed the rejection, and **exited regardless**, so it wrote no successor and produced no tokens.
**The chain survived only because slice 811 had already queued its own dependency-held successor at
slice start.** That is luck, not design: a refusal arriving when the queue is full would have ended the
midtrain silently.
✅ Fixed at **both** refusal sites in all four launchers (blacklist path and pre-flight path, 2 per
file, md5-verified): capture the `qsub` output, `exit 0` **only** if it looks like a job id
(`*[0-9].polaris-pbs*`), otherwise print `REQUEUE FAILED … NOT exiting` and **fall through to train**.
Same 84%-beats-0% arithmetic as §M+261a's bound, applied to a different failure. Discriminator
exercised as real bash on a real job id, the real rejection string, and empty input.
⚠️ Slice 811 refused on the **retired** verdict (§M+284) because its job was submitted at 04:22, before
the 04:35 neutralisation, spool timing, not a live defect. Slice 812 carries the neutralised version
and is training on `x3001c0s1b1n0`/`x3001c0s7b0n0`.
⭐ **And note which guard caught this: none of them.** It surfaced because I read the log of a slice
that was merely *missing* from the per-slice table (§M+287's n≥5 filter had quietly dropped 811).
A gap in a numbered sequence is a signal; the table that hid it was mine.

barren slice is the refusal path working as designed**, it is supposed to spend one occasionally to
escape a bad node. A RUN of them is the abort loop. Escalates at **≥2 of 6**, a bar taken from the

`grep -l 'slice .* ended'`, but **a barren slice never prints that line; it comes after training.**

`✅ none barren` while five barren slices sat inside one of them. Found by running it over a window
that provably contained them, which is the [a-checker-inherits-its-authors-blind-spot] instruction:

### §M+289a: the new check's first live output was a NEEDS ATTENTION about an already-fixed cause. Watermarked. 2026-09-16 05:4x CDT.

`barren_slices.sh` went into blockers and immediately printed
**`NEEDS ATTENTION: an ABORT LOOP is burning slices -- 3 of the last 5 finished slices produced ZERO
steps`**. Every word true, and **all three were caused by the clock verdict retired at 04:35**, so the
alarm would have kept firing for hours about something already fixed. That is the failure this record
keeps paying for: *a warning that fires on the expected case trains the reader to ignore the real one.*
⭐ **The honest fix is a WATERMARK, not a looser threshold.** `$R/.barren_ack` holds a unix timestamp;
only slices whose log is newer are counted, and the excluded count is **printed** so the exclusion is
visible rather than hidden. Set to **2026-09-16 04:35 CDT**, the moment the offending verdict was
neutralised. Widening the bar instead would have blinded the check to a genuine future loop of the
same size: the thing it exists for.
✅ Verified it is silenced, not disabled: with the watermark set, `N=12` reports **1 of 2, by design,
no escalation**; with the watermark forced to **0**, the same command reports **⛔ 5 of 11** and lists
them. A check that cannot be shown to still fire is indistinguishable from one that was turned off.
⚠️ Stated rather than papered over: the watermark cuts on **log time**, so it cannot know that slice
811, which started *after* 04:35, was still caused by the retired verdict, because its job had
spooled at 04:22. It therefore counts as one by-design refusal and will roll out of the 6-slice window
on its own. I did not move the watermark to erase it; tuning a watermark to hide one known case is how
a watermark becomes a mute button.

`RESUME=$(ls -t $R/ckpt_anneal/checkpoint_step_*.pt | head -1)`, so it depends entirely on phase A's
*last* `.pt` being the post-cooldown one. If the completion path only exported HF weights, the newest
`.pt` could be up to a full `checkpoint_interval` **before** the end of the cooldown, and on a WSD
schedule the cooldown is the part that matters most. Checked the code rather than assuming:
`continue_pretrain.py:1218` calls **`save_checkpoint(...)` FIRST**, prints `Final checkpoint saved:`,
*then* exports to `final_model_dir`, *then* writes the completion marker. So the newest `.pt` is the
final post-cooldown state **with optimizer state**, and latest-only retention keeps exactly it.
⇒ Phase B resumes from the right weights, and the marker cannot appear before them.

### §M+299: the experiment chain would have held Polaris's ONE queue slot forever. Chain only when there is work; mark when there is not. 2026-09-16 08:0x CDT.

chain once *"made the experiment line DIE SILENTLY every time the arm queue ran dry"*. That reasoning
is sound and it was written for **midway3**, where a no-op successor costs nothing.
⛔ **On Polaris it is harmful.** `debug` allows exactly ONE job per user in Q/W (§M+297, proven by
experiment), and a successor that finds 0 arms *"exits in seconds"* and then chains another: a fast
unbounded loop that **holds that single slot forever.** Consequence: the trainer's gap-filler could
never be re-parked, so the insurance invariant I added **this same hour** could never be satisfied. Two
of my own mechanisms in direct conflict, and the conflict is invisible until Sophia's boundary arrives.
✅ **Fix keeps the lesson and drops the loop:** chain only when `PENDING > 0`; when it is 0, write
`$R/.exp_line_dry` and stop. **Silence was the actual defect in the old conditional version, not the
condition.** So the marker is the part that makes the condition safe.
✅ `blockers.sh` surfaces it as `NEEDS ATTENTION: the POLARIS experiment line is DRY and did not chain`,
carrying the restart recipe (`stage_arms.sh <cell>` then submit). Verified both directions: marker
present → 1 line, absent → 0. Old script kept as `exp4gpu_dbg.pbs.pre_drymarker`; local and remote
md5 match (`217bb7d48b68`).

### §M+303: the timezone slip is now a memory entry, because it has happened twice in one day. 2026-09-16 09:2x CDT.

Two 5-hour errors on 2026-09-16 (§M+279's estimated-start read and §M+302's session-end read) share one
mechanical cause, and it is not "I forgot to use Chicago time": I *did* wrap the output in
`TZ=America/Chicago`:
⛔ **`qstat -f` prints NAIVE timestamps with no zone (`stime = Wed Sep 16 13:52:50 2026`) and they are
UTC. `date -d "<that string> + 60 minutes"` assumes LOCAL**, so the result is off by the full offset: 
and my `TZ=` wrapper then appends a correct-looking `CDT`. **It looks right.** That is why the rule
"always print Chicago time" did not prevent it: the output format was never the problem.

`date -d "<string> UTC"` or `TZ=UTC date -d "<string>" +%s`, because `TZ=America/Chicago date -d` only
*labels*, it does not convert.

already know.** `stime = 07:26` on a slice I had watched running at 02:26 CDT settles the question in
one step; no amount of reasoning about which clock a scheduler uses is as good as one matched pair.

| | optimizer state |
| --- | --- |
| muon config (the one that FITS, at hbm 95.9%): 81.2% on Muon (1 fp32 momentum) + 18.8% on AdamW (2 moments) | **9.8 GB** |
| AdamW-everything: 2 fp32 moments on all 2.06B params | **16.5 GB** |
| delta | **+6.7 GB** |

> chunking** (it uses the model's fused CE), so the teacher weights + top-K buffers are unrecoverable
> there. The recorded probe cell ran on **A40-48GB**."*
It even names the same failure magnitude I hit: *"OOM'd by 70 MiB"* versus my
*"Tried to allocate 70.00 MiB"*. ⭐ **The lesson is not "check memory first": I did the arithmetic
eventually. It is that the queue's OWN deferred/blocked arms are a record of what has already been
tried, and I deferred four of them without reading their notes.** `blocked/` is not a parking lot; it
is a list of things that do not work and why.

and KD is a −0.26 lever, so an AdamW half without KD cannot be compared to a Muon half with it. The

### §M+307: the deferred deep arm was **arithmetically impossible**, which is why it had never run. Corrected and staged. 2026-09-16 10:2x CDT.

`n730_32L_h400_s460`: the **param-matched deep arm**, i.e. the entire point of the n729/730/731 cell, 
failed twice in 30 s and went to `failed/`:
```
ValueError: num_attention_heads must be divisible by num_key_value_heads
```
Its shape is `d2304 / L32 / heads 9 / kv 2`. head_dim 2304/9 = 256 is fine, but **9 % 2 = 1**, so GQA
refuses it. ⇒ **The arm could never have run**, on any card, in any queue. That is why it sat in
`deferred/` untouched: an arm that has never executed has never been validated, and `deferred/` looked
like a parking lot rather than what it is.
⭐ **head_dim 256 forces `heads = d/256`, so with `kv = 2` the head count must be EVEN**: a constraint
worth stating plainly, because it silently rules out every width that is an odd multiple of 256
(2304, 2816, 3328 …).

✅ **Corrected as `n730b_32L_d2560_h400_s460`, and I took the cleaner of the two legal options:**
| option | shape | params vs control | what moves |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| d2048 / h8 / L32 / inter 7209 | legal | +0.006% | depth **and** width **and** head count |
| **d2560 / h10 / L32 / inter 4768** | legal | **exact: 2,063,400,960** | **depth and MLP width only** |
The control `n729` is d2560/h10/L24/inter7040, so option 2 holds `d`, `heads`, `head_dim` and `kv`
fixed and buys the extra 8 layers by shrinking `intermediate_size`. That is what *"DEPTH AT FIXED
PARAMETERS"* should mean; the d2048 variant would have moved three things at once and confounded the
reading. (The campaign's own blocked `n376_adamw_deep32_d2048` used the d2048 width, so that remains
the alternative if a future cell wants it.)

control `24 × 9600 = 230k` vs deep `32 × 7328 = 234k`, **+1.7%**, so it fits the same card the control
already fills at 95.9%. `kd_alpha 0.0`, `checkpoint_stride 1` inherited.

### §M+313: the 5th "monitor pinned to a host": the PRIMARY ran no per-GPU sampler at all, and the blacklist dropped the very node it was built to catch
**Found by reading the tick's own output for what was MISSING rather than what was wrong.** HBM has
been blank in every tick since the trainer moved to Sophia at 06:00, and `clock_census.sh` printed a
clean ✅ every 15 minutes. Both were artefacts of the same fact: `anneal_chain_sn.pbs`, the primary,
which carries >95% of phase A: had **0 matches for `nvidia-smi`**. Only the Polaris gap-fillers ran
the 60 s sampler, so:
- the census read `polaris_smi_prod_*.csv` (newest: **10:20, age 399 min**) and judged a *finished
  gap-filler* while the live 8-GPU primary went unwatched. A capped A100 on sophia-gpu-01 would have
  cost ~16-22% with no symptom: the §M+261 defect, one host over.
- HBM had no source on Sophia between the python `[HBM]` prints, and the print itself landed in
  `$R/code/continue_pretrain.py` at **11:28 UTC = 06:28 CDT**, i.e. **28 minutes after slice 042
  started**, so python had already read the old file. Not a bug: the patch reaches the next slice: 
  but it means the field stays blank for ~5 h and the reason has to be said, not inferred.
- ⛔ **The census header had already PRESCRIBED the fix** ("If a clock cap is ever suspected on Sophia,
  the fix is to add a sampler to its chain, not to widen this script") and even recorded the
  consequence of not doing it ("silence from a host-pinned monitor reads exactly like a clean result",
  §M+292). **Writing the post-mortem did not add the sampler.** It sat unwritten for a day.

**Fixed, three parts, each with its reader:**
1. `anneal_chain_sn.pbs` now starts the same sampler (identical 6-field schema, so one parser serves
   both hosts) and kills it after `torchrun`. `bash -n` clean; md5 `834196c902884b5eaa0572cfbea71065`;
   original kept as `.pre_smi`. PBS spools at submit, so it reaches the slice after `186168`/`186178`.
2. `clock_census.sh` follows `$H` (blockers passes the host `trainer_status.sh` resolved) and globs
   `*_smi_prod_*.csv`. **Widening the glob ALONE would have been the same lie with a wider mouth**: 
   it would have read the stale Polaris csv and declared Sophia healthy, so a **staleness gate** now
   returns `NO VERDICT` above `MAXAGE=900 s`, naming the age and the host.
3. `blockers.sh` reports the `NO VERDICT` state as info. A blind monitor that prints nothing is
   indistinguishable from a healthy one, which is the whole failure being fixed.

**AND THE BACKFILL, which is the part that had a real cost already banked.** Blacklist maintenance
read only the NEWEST csv, so a capped GPU whose slice ended between two 15-minute ticks was seen by
nobody. Demonstrated, not hypothesised: a scan of all 151 csvs found **`x3001c0s13b1n0/g3` capped at
1095 MHz in 53 samples (csv 03:05)** and **absent from `$R/.slow_nodes`**, while its neighbour `b0n0`
: capped during a slice that happened to be newest at a tick, was present. The launcher would have
accepted a node this tool already had the data to refuse. Now scans a **7-day window** (measured: 44
csvs / 999 KB, 0.6 s): bounded rather than all-history so a *repaired* node re-enters the pool
without hand-editing. `$R/.slow_nodes` is now `x3001c0s13b0n0 x3001c0s13b1n0`.

**⛔ TWO OF MY OWN ERRORS INSIDE THIS ONE FIX, both of the same family:**
- **A fix with n=1, sized by what felt cheap.** The first backfill scanned the newest **8** csvs and
  found nothing: the b1n0 csv is 03:05 and sits ~15 files back, so the widened check still could not
  see the case it was written for. Measuring the cost took one command and made 7 days obviously free.
- **A multi-line list interpolated into an ssh command line.** `ssh -n host "printf '%s\n' $_BF >> $BL"`
  with a two-line `$_BF` sends the remote shell TWO commands: `printf … b0n0`, whose redirection was
  left behind on the next line, so it printed to stdout instead of appending, and `b1n0 >> $BL`,
  which it tried to **execute**. Net: the backfill dropped the one node it existed to catch, and
  **the failure looked like success** (the tick still printed a blacklist line). Feed lists on stdin;
  and drop `-n`, which points stdin at `/dev/null`: the same trap as before.
- Both directions tested at the real call site: a stale csv → `NO VERDICT`; the 07:26 fixture with the
  known cap → `⛔ CAPPED x3001c0s13b0n0/g3`, blacklist appended idempotently.

### §M+314: phase B's data was NOT "two numbers plus flatten": the length filter is a real pass, and the threshold should be 2× the block size. Built and staged. 2026-09-16 12:5x, 13:1x CDT.
**The gate that would have caught this at handover, ~3 days from now, is the one that made me look:**
`ctx_chain_sn.pbs` refuses unless `$R/data/ctx_mix/ctx_mix_flat.bin` exists, and it does not exist.
So phase A ends in ~3.1 days into a machine with nothing to run. §M+286 had concluded the remaining
work was "two `budget_tokens` values, plus flatten"; it named one deferred mechanical unknown: 
whether the builder accepts a pre-tokenized source, and said to settle it *with a command*. Settled:

**✅ The "no re-tokenization" half is TRUE.** `cmd_flatten` globs `$RC_OUT_ROOT/<name>/*.bin`, memmaps
each as raw `uint32` and interleaves weighted-fair. It needs only `tier` + `budget_tokens` in the
registry. Layout verified on two shards: `bytes/4 == sum(lengths)` exactly, **no header** (the flat
llm.c `.bin` has a 1024-byte header; a **docbin shard does not**: conflating them would have shifted
every document by 256 tokens). Lengths live in `*.lengths.npy`, so the `*.bin` glob cannot pick them
up by accident.

**⛔ The other half was WRONG, in the one way that matters: `min_doc_tokens` is a TOKENIZE-time
filter.** `cmd_flatten` never reads it, never reads `_source_manifest.json`, and has **no per-doc
awareness at all**. So on a pre-tokenized source, setting `min_doc_tokens=13568` in the registry
does **nothing**, and phase B would have trained at block 13,568 over a stream whose windows mostly
straddle document boundaries, which is the exact failure the data gate warns about in as many words
("would be 'extending context' over padding and would look like it worked"). A knob that is inert on
the path you are using is [[sliding-window-inert-in-production]] again, one tree over.

**⭐ AND THE THRESHOLD SHOULD BE 2× THE BLOCK SIZE, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED.** Exact, from the
`.lengths.npy` arrays alone (no token I/O): "single-doc windows" = P(a uniformly chosen 13,568-token
window lies inside ONE document) = `Σ max(0, L−B+1) / Σ L`.
| filter | docs | tokens | single-doc windows | median doc |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| all | 1,542,673 | 28.633B | **41.6%** | 13,668 |
| ≥ 13,568 (1×B) | 777,690 | 22.459B | **53.0%** | 22,417 |
| ≥ 27,136 (2×B) | 274,362 | 12.860B | **71.1%** | 37,624 |
| ≥ 54,272 (4×B) | 56,171 | 4.925B | 84.5% | 70,646 |
The planned 1×B filter buys almost nothing (41.6 → 53.0%) because a document of exactly one window
still straddles unless the stream offset happens to align to it. **2×B buys 71.1% and still leaves
12.860B tokens ≈ 2.1× phase B's ~6.0B budget**; 4×B is purer but **under** budget, so it is not a
candidate. `--min_tokens` is a flag, not a constant, because that trade is the arguable part.

**Built, not just planned:** `reasoning/filter_docbin_by_length.py` (new) → `sbatch ctx_filter.sbatch`
on `amd`/`rcc-staff`, 1 core / 6G / `Gres=(null)` node, **completed in 2m02s**, MaxRSS **454 MB**
(6G was over-asked; 1G is the right number, recorded for the next one). Output
`/project/rcc/youzhi/data/reasoning_anneal/longctx_arxiv` = **274,362 docs / 12.860B tokens / 48 GB /
100 shards**, exactly the figure the lengths arrays predicted. Registry entry `longctx_arxiv` added
(`enabled=False`, so it can never silently join a rebuild of the phase-A corpus mid-run;
`budget_tokens=0` reads as "ratio unchosen": ⚠️ flatten treats 0 as *use everything*, so the
`--budgets` number is mandatory, not optional). Verified at the real call site: flatten's own
`source_outdir()` sees **100 bins**.
- **Correctness check that actually proves it, rather than counting:** token-identity against the
  source at the **first, second, middle and LAST** kept document (the last is what catches an
  off-by-one the first never would): all identical, lengths array exact. The script re-validates
  `bytes/4 == Σ lengths` per shard and refuses the whole run if a layout ever changes, because a
  silent offset error here produces a corpus no downstream check would catch.
- ⚠️ `set -euo pipefail` **killed the first submission in 3 s**: the AI conda env's `activate.d` hook
  trips `ADDR2LINE: unbound variable` under `nounset`. Activate first, then `set -eo pipefail`. The
  env a job runs in is part of the job.
- ⚠️ Remaining ordering bias, stated not fixed: flatten consumes a source's shards in sorted order,
  so a 4B budget against a 12.86B pool reads only `arXiv_000..030`-ish, which is chronological.
  Worth a shuffle of the shard list if the arxiv budget lands well under the pool.
- ⚠️ `--cooldown 1658` in `ctx_chain_sn.pbs` encodes **11,053 steps = 6.0B tokens** at
  `total_batch_size 542720`, and there is no `--train_tokens`: with `--max_epochs 1` **the corpus
  size IS the run length**, so the mix total and the cooldown must move together or the WSD schedule
  silently changes shape. Same family as the `--cooldown 0` bug.
- ⚠️ Superseding a directive out loud, per §M+286: the arxiv source was deliberately kept out of
  `build_reasoning_corpus.py` (owner, 2026-07-29, "get the DATA ready but do NOT wire it in").
  Wiring it in is a working-tree edit with no commit, and it is `enabled=False`.
⇒ **What is left for phase B is now genuinely two numbers plus flatten**, and a ~50 GB relay to
/eagle. The ratio still waits on phase A's curve, by design.

### §M+315: the monitor reported a 3.3× throughput collapse on a healthy trainer, because tqdm's rate field is an EMA and a checkpoint save poisons it. 2026-09-16 12:5x CDT.
`trainer_status.sh` printed **31.79 s/step / 17,007 tok/s / 2,125 per GPU**: against the recorded
9.52 / 56,793 / 7,099, while **its own step delta in the same line** said `+60 steps in 9m` = 9.0
s/step. The save log settles it: step 208361 saved at 12:51 CDT, retention pruned 208172 (23.1 GiB
freed, latest-only working as designed), and the tqdm field was still unwinding: **31.79 → 25.11 →
20.44**. A 24.76 GB ZeRO save costs ~269 s with no steps, so tqdm's EMA spikes and decays for
minutes afterwards.
- **Why it matters rather than being cosmetic:** at `--checkpoint_interval 3600` the poisoned window
  is ~8% of every hour, so roughly **1 tick in 12** would print a catastrophic-looking rate, and the
  obvious response to a 3× slowdown is to kill and re-shape a job that is completely fine. The step
  counter is ground truth; the rate field is decoration.
- ⛔ **MY FIRST FIX WAS WRONG AND ITS OWN THIRD TEST CASE REFUTED IT.** "Trust the step delta" printed
  **50.00 s/step** for 6 steps in 5 minutes while tqdm correctly read 9.52. **Both fields are
  distorted by a save, in OPPOSITE directions:** a window *containing* the save has too few steps
  (delta reads slow); a window *just after* it has an EMA still unwinding (tqdm reads slow). Neither
  is the steady-state rate. Picking the wrong one of two wrong numbers is worse than showing the
  disagreement, this is [[a-checker-inherits-its-authors-blind-spot]] with the checker written
  ninety seconds after the diagnosis.
- **Shipped:** when the two disagree by >1.25×, print both labelled, `X s/step eff / Y inst`, tok/s
  from the effective rate (it is what sets the ETA, save overhead included), and name the cause.
  Otherwise unchanged. Gated on `D>=5 && MINS>=5`. Three cases tested: just-after-save (3.5×,
  reports both), healthy (unchanged single number), window-contains-save (5.3×, reports both).

### §M+316: phase B's "disjoint reasoning slice" DOES NOT NEED BUILDING: it was built in July and is 6.022B tokens. 2026-09-16 12:5x CDT.
The phase-B data gate asks for "long-doc arxiv + a **DISJOINT** reasoning slice". Chased the
disjointness question and it is already answered on disk.
- ⚠️ **My first pass got it wrong in the standard way**: I compared each source's on-disk `.bin`
  total against its **registry `budget_tokens`** and concluded the surplus was **0.607B**, i.e. that a
  disjoint anchor was essentially unavailable. That is [[which-statistic-is-this-number]]: the
  registry budget is not what the phase-A flatten consumed. The flat corpus is **18.066B** tokens
  (72,265,290,056 B / 4, matching `anneal_dup_probe.py`'s asserted 18,066,322,258), while the
  registry budgets sum to 44.088B, and `fineweb_edu_a4` (20.6B) was added **five days after** that
  flatten, so it was never in it.
- ⭐ **What actually happened:** the non-a4 sources hold **24.089B** tokens and the Jul-15 flatten ran
  `--holdout_frac 0.25 --part main` → 24.089 × 0.75 = **18.067B = the phase-A corpus, exactly**. The
  remaining 25% is `reasoning_midtrain_flat.bin`, **24,088,430,696 B = 6.022B tokens** = 24.089 × 0.25.
- **Confirmed by provenance, not only by the arithmetic** (an exact match with a known figure is not
  by itself evidence): `run_full_training.a35.sh:339-344` states it in as many words, phase A reads
  the first 75%, the holdout is `reasoning_midtrain_flat.bin`, and "the two share NO source tokens
  (main=[0,split), holdout=[split,use) per flatten)". Size unchanged since July and it matches the
  figure recorded independently in `A5_KD_RECIPE.md:822`.
⇒ **Phase B's data work is now: two budget numbers, one flatten, one ~24 GB relay.** Nothing to build.
- ⚠️ **But not one flatten call as-is.** `--part`/`--holdout_frac` are GLOBAL, not per-source, so
  `--part holdout` (needed to keep the reasoning window disjoint) also takes only the last 25% of the
  arxiv pool: with `--budgets longctx_arxiv=N` the arxiv contribution is **0.25 × N**, so N must be
  4× the intended arxiv tokens (12.86B pool ⇒ ≤3.2B of arxiv reachable this way). That is the
  zero-new-code path. If the chosen ratio wants more arxiv than 3.2B, the alternative is a per-source
  `part` override: a small edit, named here so it is not rediscovered at handover.
- ⛔ Do NOT instead concatenate two finished flats: flatten's chunk-granular weighted interleave is
  what keeps sources mixed THROUGHOUT, and sequential concatenation is the §13 forgetting mode.

### §M+318: ran the phase-B flatten instead of reasoning about it, and it refuted §M+316's "zero new code": the disjointness knob is per-source or it is nothing. 2026-09-16 13:2x CDT.
A 25M-token dry run into scratch (never into `$DATA`: see the gate note below) proved the mechanical
half outright: `longctx_arxiv` is readable by flatten (**100 bins, avail 12.860B**, matching the
filter's own total), `--include` is required and works for an `enabled=False` source, the emitted
ratios match the budgets exactly, the output carries the flat llm.c header
(100,001,024 B = 25,000,000 × 4 + 1024), and throughput is **3.5-4.3M tok/s ⇒ a 6.0B mix flattens in
~23-29 min**. §M+316's prediction that `--part holdout` yields **0.25 × N** on the arxiv pool was
confirmed by the command.
**⛔ AND THE DRY RUN EXPOSED WHAT READING COULD NOT: "holdout" IS NOT A GUARANTEE OF DISJOINTNESS.**
`split` is computed from `use = min(avail, budget)`, so a smaller budget than the earlier run's moves
the split EARLIER and the resulting "holdout" lands **inside phase A's main window**: silently
re-serving trained tokens, which is precisely the repetition failure the phase-B gate exists to
prevent. My first dry run did exactly that: `github_code=20000000` produced `window=[0.015B,0.020B)`,
deep inside phase A's `[0, 6.0B)`. **The rule: pass each reasoning source the SAME budget phase A
used (the registry values reproduce it, since `use=min(avail,budget)`), and shrink a source's
contribution with a skip, never by lowering its budget.** Written into the code at the split.
**And the global flags cannot express phase B's mix at all.** `--part`/`--skip_frac` apply to every
source, but phase B needs the *holdout* of sources phase A already read the main 75% of, mixed with
*all* of a long-context source phase A never touched, and with the reasoning side pinned at exactly
0.25 × budget (= 6.02B, the entire phase-B budget) there is no room for arxiv. So `--parts` and
`--skips` (per-source, same `name=value` style as `--budgets`, falling back to the globals) were
added, with validation that rejects a bad part value and an unknown source name. Verified on the real
shape: arxiv `part=all window=[0,0.030B)`, `github_code part=holdout skip=0.995
window=[7.990B,8.000B)`, `am_r1 window=[2.944B,2.948B)`: inside the last 25%, i.e. genuinely
disjoint, shrunk without moving the split.
⇒ §M+316's "two numbers, one flatten, one relay" is now TRUE, but only because the missing knob was
built. The ratio is still the only open decision.
**⚠️ AND A GATE THAT WOULD HAVE LET A TRUNCATED CORPUS THROUGH.** `ctx_chain_sn.pbs` tested
`[ ! -s "$DATA" ]`, which passes on **any non-empty file**, so a flatten that died half-way, or one
written straight to `$DATA` rather than to a temp name and renamed, would have started phase B on a
partial corpus and looked like it worked. Added a size floor: the mix is ~6.0B tokens ≈ 24 GB
(542,720 × 11,053 steps, which is what `--cooldown 1658` encodes as 15%), so **under 4 GB is a failed
build, not a small corpus**. `bash -n` clean, md5 `43bd62ca4cce56e0679174500957ea14`, original kept as
`.pre_sizegate`.

### §M+319: the running slice is still on the OLD `--checkpoint_interval`, and nothing checked that a spooled job matches the launcher on disk. 2026-09-16 13:4x CDT.
Noticed because the mirror advanced 208361 → **208550** in 20 minutes. The save steps in slice 042's
own log are dead-regular: 207605, 207794, 207983, 208172, 208361, 208550, a **189-step** spacing,
and 189 × 9.52 s = **1,799 s**. The launcher on disk says `--checkpoint_interval 3600` (raised from

around 18:00 on 09-15, at the START of the previous slice, the successor is submitted unheld to bank
`eligible_time`, which is **before** the edit. [[patching-a-script-does-not-patch-queued-jobs]],
with the twist that the unheld-successor design *guarantees* every slice's spool is ~12 h stale.
- **Cost, using the measured save time:** 269 s per save ⇒ **269/1800 = 15% of wall spent saving**

- **No action, deliberately.** Killing the running trainer to pick up a better flag forfeits up to one

  "No available resources". `186168` was queued at 06:00 today, after the edit, so it carries 3600 and

- ⭐ **The check that was missing, and the only observable that can answer it:** a config file tells
  you what the NEXT job will do; the **save spacing in the running job's own log** tells you what the
  spool is doing. `~/bin/config_drift.sh` computes it and compares, wired into `blockers.sh` as info
  (a throughput tax produces no symptoms, which is exactly why it must be printed). Bar is 1.25×
  because the tqdm s/step it multiplies is EMA-noisy (§M+315) while a 1800-vs-3600 drift is 2.0×.
- ⛔ **AND IT SHIPPED BROKEN FOR TEN MINUTES, IN THE WAY I HAVE ON RECORD.** Wired in, it printed
  **nothing**: `timeout: failed to run command '/home/youzhi/bin/config_drift.sh': Permission denied`
: the file had no **x bit**. Every test I ran used `bash ~/bin/config_drift.sh`, which does not need
  it; `blockers.sh` execs the path directly, which does. **Testing a script with an explicit
  interpreter does not test how its caller invokes it.** Found only by keeping stderr instead of
  discarding it: `2>/dev/null` on a helper call converts "cannot execute" into "nothing to report".

### §M+320: the stale spool is BY DESIGN, so numeric flags now come from a file the spool reads at RUNTIME. 2026-09-16 13:5x CDT.
§M+319 found the live slice saving every 1,799 s against a launcher that says 3600. The reason is not
carelessness: **the successor is submitted unheld at the START of the previous slice** so it can bank
`eligible_time` (`anneal_chain_sn.pbs:239-249`, itself a fix worth ~2× throughput), so **every slice
necessarily runs flags that are ~12 h old.** Two edits today already inherit it: the interval, and
the SMI sampler, which cannot go live until the slice after the two already-queued successors.
**Fix for the half that can be fixed:** a flag that is a NUMBER need not wait two slices. The launcher
now sources `$R/.tunables` at runtime and uses `$CKPT_INT` in the flag, so
`echo 'CKPT_INT=3600' > $R/.tunables` takes effect at the **very next slice**. Code changes still
wait: a sourced file cannot add a sampler, and pretending otherwise would be the more dangerous
half-fix.
- **Default is 3600 with no file present**, i.e. identical to today's behaviour, and the file is
  deliberately NOT created: a mechanism that is only exercised when something needs changing has one
  fewer moving part than one that is always on.
- **Validated because a sourced file is arbitrary shell:** a non-numeric or empty `CKPT_INT` is
  rejected back to 3600 with a log line. Four branches tested (absent / 5400 / `abc` / empty): the
  last three matter because `. file` would otherwise let a typo reach `--checkpoint_interval`, and
  argparse would take `abc` as far as an exception mid-slice.
- The effective value is echoed into the slice log next to the spool's own mtime, so the log answers
  "which config was this job actually running" without inference. `config_drift.sh` still measures the
  SAVE SPACING rather than trusting that echo: the observable beats the declaration.
- `bash -n` clean, md5 `227b95a879e8d8400822ec33268f4aa1`, original kept as `.pre_tunables`.

### §M+321: I blinded my own detector one tick after building it, for the THIRD time today, so the standing guard is now "every monitor must still produce a parseable verdict". 2026-09-16 14:1x, 14:2x CDT.
§M+320's tunables edit replaced the literal `--checkpoint_interval 3600` with `$CKPT_INT`, and
`config_drift.sh` greps that flag's TEXT. So `FLAG` went empty and the detector went **silent about a
drift that was still happening**, one tick after I wrote it. Three instances today, all the same
shape: **each fix changed an artifact that some monitor reads as its INPUT**:
| fix | monitor it blinded | how it failed |
|---|---|---|
| added the SMI sampler | `clock_census.sh` | glob still pointed at the other host's csv |
| the run changed stage | `mirror_status.sh` | reported a directory nothing writes |
| `3600` → `$CKPT_INT` | `config_drift.sh` | grep matched nothing, verdict suppressed |
All three failed silently and all three looked like a clean result.
- **Repaired:** the effective interval is now resolved the way the launcher resolves it, 
  `.tunables`, then the launcher's `CKPT_INT=` default, then a literal flag (Polaris still hardcodes
  it). Precedence tested three ways: 5400 / 3600 / 1800.
- ⛔ **And the guard lied about WHY.** With `FLAG` empty, the single combined precondition printed
  *"not enough saves yet on sophia (4 save steps)"*: sending me to look at a save count that was
  fine. Split into one guard per missing input, and the FLAG one now says outright that it is **the
  script's own bug, not the trainer's**.
- ⛔⛔ **The comment explaining the fix then caused the next bug**, because I put it INSIDE the
  double-quoted ssh payload, where `#` is not a comment: naming the variable with its sigil made the
  LOCAL shell expand it, and under `set -u` every run printed
  `config_drift.sh: line 43: CKPT_INT: unbound variable`, invisible, because `blockers.sh` calls it
  with `2>/dev/null`. Same family as "never put a backtick-comment inside a python arg list". Prose
  belongs outside the quotes.

**THE STRUCTURAL FIX, since three instances in one day is a pattern and not bad luck:**
`recipe_smoke.sh` (hourly cron, reports through the marker `blockers.sh` surfaces) now runs all five
tick-critical monitors: `trainer_status`, `config_drift`, `clock_census`, `mirror_status`,
`stage_now`, and requires each to say something self-identifying.
- ⭐ **Deliberately NOT an "is the answer good" check.** "no capped GPU", "NO VERDICT" and "in sync"
  are all legitimate. It trips on the three shapes that mean **the tool** is broken: empty output, a
  shell-level error (`Permission denied`, `unbound variable`, `command not found`, `syntax error`,
  `No such file`), or a monitor reporting it could not resolve its own input.
- ⭐ **That bar is also why a cluster outage cannot trip it:** an unreachable host still produces a
  worded verdict, which a reachability-based bar would have flagged as broken.
- It earned itself immediately: its first run surfaced the `unbound variable` above, which had been
  swallowed by `2>/dev/null` on every tick. **A guard that catches a live bug in its first execution
  is the only kind worth adding.**

### §M+323: the bounded-refusal guard was not bounded "in a row": nothing ever reset the strike counter, so three refusals over any timespan would have disabled it permanently. 2026-09-16 14:4x CDT.
Checked the reader of an artifact I changed today: `.slow_nodes` went from one node to two (§M+313)
, and the reader is fine: `grep -x -F -f "$BLFILE"` against the sorted nodefile is a per-line fixed
match, so a multi-entry blacklist works by construction. Verified both directions against the real
two-line file: a nodefile containing `x3001c0s13b1n0` hits, a clean one returns empty.
**But the same block revealed a live defect.** `$R/.preflight_refusals` is incremented on every
refusal and its message says *"drawn $PFN times in a row"*, and a grep across every `.pbs` and
every script in `~/bin` found **zero writers besides the increment**. The counter is MONOTONE over
the whole run, so after three refusals spread over any number of days, not three consecutive: the
bound flips permanently to `TRAINING ANYWAY` on a clock-capped node. That is the worst of the three
possible states: **it reads as protected and is not**, and the symptom is a silent 16% tax.
- The implementation contradicted its own stated semantics, which is how it survived review: the
  message asserts the property the code does not have.
- **Fixed in all four launchers that carry the block** (`anneal_polaris_dbg2`, `anneal_polaris_dbg`,
  `anneal_polaris`, `ctx_polaris_dbg2`): the class, not the instance: a clean node draw clears the
  counter and logs how many strikes it cleared. `bash -n` clean on all four, originals kept as
  `.pre_pfreset`. Reaches the next submission; `7628003` is already spooled but the counter is at 0
  (absent), so it has its full three strikes.
- **Failure direction reasoned explicitly, because both directions are wrong in different amounts:**
  an over-eager reset costs one extra refusal (~1 min of requeue); a missing reset costs the guard
  entirely. Reset on clean.
- ⚠️ **My first test harness fooled itself and I nearly shipped on its verdict.** `bash -c '...'
  HIT="$H"` sets **`$0`**, not the variable, so `$HIT` was unset inside, `${HIT// /}` was empty, and
  the "hit-present" case reported the reset firing when a node WAS blacklisted, i.e. the harness
  produced the exact false result that would have condemned correct code. Re-run with `HIT=` as an
  environment assignment, all three states behave: clear-with-counter, clear-without, and refusal
  keeps the count at 1. **A negative test that passes for the wrong reason is worse than no test**,
  and this is the second harness error today (§M+317's `MIRROR_LAG_STEPS=1` proved nothing).

### §M+329: the drift detector inherited the EMA poisoning I had fixed in the other consumer an hour earlier. 2026-09-16 16:0x CDT.
`config_drift.sh` reported the save interval as **1799 → 2492 → 1916 s** on three consecutive ticks
for a job whose interval never changed. It multiplied `189 steps x <the tqdm s/step field>`, and that
field is an EMA a save poisons for minutes (§M+315), so the answer swung with where in the save cycle
the tick happened to land. **I had fixed exactly this in `trainer_status.sh` and never asked who else
read the same field**, which is [[a-checker-inherits-its-authors-blind-spot]]'s "after you fix
something, grep every consumer" failing on the next script I wrote.
**Fixed by removing the rate from the calculation entirely.** A save STALLS the training loop, so it appears as
a gap in tqdm's own ELAPSED clock; the mean elapsed distance between consecutive gaps is the realised
cycle, in seconds, with no rate and no step arithmetic. Now stable at **~1792 s** against a configured
1800.
- ⛔ **My first attempt failed silently into the old path, which is the worse outcome.** I tried to
  index the elapsed clock by the checkpoint's step, but a checkpoint is named with the **GLOBAL** step
  (209495) while tqdm counts **LOCAL** phase-A steps (6055/33414), an offset of 203,440 here. Nothing
  matched, `$OBS` came back empty, and the script fell back to the EMA path: the fix looked applied and
  was not. **Two numberings that both look like "the step" is a parse question, not a detail.**
- ⚠️ **And the raw gap-to-gap distance is interval + save, not interval.** It measured 1876 s;
  1800 + 84 = 1884 is 0.4% off while the bare 1800 is 4.2% off, which is also the evidence that the
  timer is end-referenced. Subtracting `SAVE_S` compares like with like against the flag, without it
  a correctly configured job would have read 4% adrift forever.
- Verified at the real call site through `blockers.sh`, not just standalone.

action never fires.** It would have printed `info` for hours.

is normal (§M+114 measured 0-1 min). Tens of minutes means the node went to a competitor *and* the
Polaris gap-filler is not carrying it either: "no trainer anywhere" already covers the insurance,
since a Polaris slice IS a trainer. So a watermark records when the no-trainer state began and the
line escalates from `info` to `NEEDS ATTENTION` at `MAX_GAP_MIN=15`, naming what to check (rival
`eligible_time`, and whether the parked gap-filler woke).

`add_argument` under any spelling (`log_interval`, `log-interval`, `log_every`, `logging_steps`), and
the anneal launcher passes none. I ported the block from `pretrain.py`, which DOES define it
(`uses=2 defines=1`, verified).
**And the dereference sat in the `if` CONDITION: OUTSIDE the `try` that existed to make HBM
observability harmless.** So slice 043 would have raised `AttributeError` on its first logging step:
the trainer dies **at the handover**, and a diagnostic added to watch the run takes the run down.
Slice 042 is unaffected because Python read and compiled the file at 11:00 UTC, 28 min before the

**Fixed in BOTH trees** (`$R/code/` md5 `0fdf2ce7fe6452e35a3152cf22dc0ac1`, local
`ca9ddd6ec28d4e32efc20ee7e7148a09`, `.pre_hbmfix` kept): `getattr(args, "log_interval", 25)` **and the
guard moved inside the `try`**, because *a condition is part of the diagnostic* and the rule is that a
diagnostic must never be able to kill the run. `py_compile` clean; `__pycache__` removed.
- ⭐ **What found it was asking "will the thing I added actually produce output?" rather than "did my
  edit land?"** The edit landed perfectly, md5-verified, in the right file, in the right tree, and was

### §M+334: the resume path picked the newest-MODIFIED checkpoint, not the highest step, five lines above a function that does it correctly. 2026-09-16 17:1x CDT.
Final pre-boundary check: where will slice 043 resume from? The selection was
`RESUME=$(ls -t $R/ckpt_anneal/checkpoint_step_*.pt | head -1)`: **mtime order**, while `cur_step()`,
defined **five lines below it**, answers the same question the right way
(`sed 's/.*step_//' | sort -n | tail -1`). Two idioms for one question, with the weaker one on the
line that decides where training resumes.
**Why mtime is the wrong key here, concretely:** anything that touches an older checkpoint, a restore
from the offsite mirror, a filesystem copy, a promoted `.tmp`: makes it the newest by mtime, and the
chain would resume from it and **discard every step since, while training continues happily**. There
is no symptom: the loss is fine, the rate is fine, the step counter simply goes backwards once and
nobody is watching the absolute number at a handover. (The mirror does create hardlinks in that dir: 
`.mirror_stage_NNNNN.pt`, but they share the inode, so they cannot change an original's mtime, and
the glob prefix does not match them. Checked rather than assumed.)
**Fixed** to pick the highest step with an existence test, keeping the mtime form as a fallback; md5
`b663ad9bfee1966fa3efdb8633f9b37b`, `.pre_resumefix` kept, `bash -n` clean. Both idioms agree today
(`checkpoint_step_209873.pt`), which is why this was invisible. PBS spools at submit, so this reaches
the slice after `186168`/`186246`: tonight's handover still uses the mtime form, and the two agree.
⭐ **The pattern worth naming: when one file contains two ways to compute the same thing, the weaker
one is a latent bug, and the stronger one right next to it is the proof that somebody already knew.**

### §M+338: the ordering experiment is SETTLED and it refutes both of my models: the node went to a 1-HOUR job. Backfill, not FIFO and not eligible_time. 2026-09-16 18:1x CDT.
`sophia-gpu-01` freed at 17:30 and went to **`186278`**, pranavviswanath, `by-node`, **1 node,
`walltime = 01:00:00`**, `stime = 22:35:17 UTC`. That single fact kills both models I had been using:
- **Not FIFO:** xiaolongm holds ~20 queued 1-node `by-node` jobs with ids from 185476 up, all older.
- **Not `eligible_time`:** `186166` had banked 8:57:57; `186278` was submitted hours later.
- **What distinguishes the winner is its WALL:** 1 h against xiaolongm's 24 h and our 12 h/24 h. That
  is **backfill**: a short job fits a window that a long one cannot, so PBS slots it in ahead of
  everything older. §M+332 was right to refuse to assert FIFO; the answer was a third mechanism.
**⇒ The tempting action is to shorten our Sophia request, and the arithmetic says DON'T.** Measured on
slice 817 rather than assumed: job start → training loop = **175 s** (module load, data mmap, 24.76 GB
checkpoint load), first-step `torch.compile` = **93 s** (129 steps in 1,466 s of loop time at a 10.64
s/step steady rate ⇒ 1466 − 129×10.64 = 93), wall-save reserve 180 s. So **~268 s of fixed cost per
slice, not the ~7 min on record**: worth correcting in its own right.
| shape | steps/slice | **steps per hour of wall** |
|---|---|---|
| Sophia 12 h slice | 4,489 | **374** |
| Sophia 1 h slices | 330 | **330** |
| Polaris 1 h slices (current) | 295 | **295** |
A 1 h Sophia chain would beat Polaris by **+12%**, but it is **−12% against the 12 h Sophia slice we
already have queued**, and a short job of ours could backfill into exactly the window the 12 h job
needs, locking us into the worse mode by our own hand. The 12 h request costs nothing to leave queued.
⇒ **No action: keep the long requests queued, let Polaris carry.** Recorded because the lever is real,
attractive, and wrong here, and because the next person to see a 1 h job jump a 20-deep queue should
find the arithmetic rather than re-derive it.
⚠️ Corollary for anything we ever DO want placed on a busy Sophia (a probe, an eval, a one-off): ask
for the shortest wall that fits the work. That is what wins, not patience.

### §M+340: ⛔ RETRACTION of §M+339's opening claim: `preemptable` is still unusable, and I mis-parsed the same field twice in five minutes, in OPPOSITE directions. 2026-09-16 18:4x CDT.
I built `exp4gpu_pre.pbs` (a `-q preemptable`, 1-node, 2 h copy of the debug session launcher, with the
hardcoded self-chain rewritten so it cannot steal the trainer's `debug` slot: `bash -n` clean, diff
reviewed, 4 substantive lines changed) and submitted it as **`7628722`**. PBS answered:
`comment = Not Running: Insufficient amount of resource: queue_tags`
: **the exact failure [[polaris-preemptable-is-a-dead-queue]] records.** Per the standing prompt's
"do not leave tag-starved jobs queued for hours; qdel them", cancelled it immediately. Net cost: one
launcher that is now built and correct if the tag situation ever changes, and ~6 minutes.
**⛔ AND THE EVIDENCE I ACTED ON WAS A PARSE ERROR: TWICE, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS:**
1. §M+339 said "one free node carries the `preemptable` tag" from an `awk` over `pbsnodes -a` whose
   `state` and `queue_tags` could come from **different node blocks** (attributes are alphabetical, so
   `queue_tags` precedes `state`). A per-node-correct re-parse then said **two**.
2. Doubting that, I read one node directly, and got `queue_tags = demand`, which "proved" the census
   wrong. **That read was the broken one:** my pipeline did `tr "," "\n"` FIRST, so
   `queue_tags = demand,preemptable` split into `demand` and a bare `preemptable`, and the grep kept
   only the first half. The authoritative read is `resources_available.queue_tags = demand,preemptable`.
⇒ **Both nodes really are free, really are `system=polaris`, really carry the tag, and a
`preemptable` job still cannot place on them.** The queue requests the literal `queue_tags = preemptable`
while the node advertises `demand,preemptable`, and `debug` jobs DO place on `prod,debug` nodes, so the
matching rule is not simple membership. **I am not chasing the mechanism further**: the memory already
prices that chase at a 4-hour trainer gap, and the operational answer is settled either way.
⭐ **The lesson is about the order of operations in a pipeline, not about PBS.** A transform that
*splits* a field (`tr ","`) must not run before the filter that *identifies* it, or the filter reads
half a value and reports it as the whole. I had `validate-the-parse-not-just-the-query` in front of me
and still built the conclusion on the two halves of one broken read.
⇒ Experiments remain on the owner's (a)-wait / (b)-debug-slot choice. The 4 arms stay staged in
`/eagle/queue/pending` (§M+339), which is the part of that work that keeps its value either way.

### §M+341: the bounded-refusal path was INERT on Polaris: its requeue fails every time, by construction, so every blacklisted draw trained degraded. 2026-09-16 18:5x CDT.
The tick opened at **12.13 s/step / 44,573 tok/s** against 10.64 / 50,815: **−14%**, with the step
delta agreeing (so real, not the EMA). The clock census named the cause in the same breath:
`⛔ CAPPED: x3001c0s13b1n0/g3`, read from the LIVE slice's own sampler. Slice 818 is on the
blacklisted node. Its log:
```
nodes: x3001c0s13b1n0 x3001c0s7b1n0
ABORT: allocated a BLACKLISTED node (x3001c0s13b1n0) … Refusal 1/3, requeueing for a different node set
REQUEUE FAILED (qsub: would exceed queue generic's per-user limit of jobs in 'Q' state) -- NOT exiting; training on this node set instead
```
**⛔ AND THE REQUEUE DOES NOT FAIL BY ACCIDENT, IT CANNOT SUCCEED.** This chain always holds a
dependency-held successor, and that job plus the running one exhaust the `generic` per-user allowance
for jobs in Q state. So `qsub` is refused on **every** refusal, and the §M+288 bound: "refuse, requeue,
and only train anyway after 3 strikes": degrades to "train anyway, always". Measured twice inside one
hour: slices **816** and **818** both drew `x3001c0s13b1n0`, both refused, both failed to requeue, both
trained at −14%. Slice 816's failure happened with only ONE held job queued, which is what rules out
my first theory that the preemptable job I submitted at 18:38 had stolen the slot.
**Fixed: a held successor IS a better requeue than a failed one.** On `REQUEUE FAILED`, if any job of
ours is in `H`, the slice now **exits**: `afterany` releases the successor immediately and it draws a
fresh node set. That is exactly the manual recovery that worked at 17:44 (clean nodes on the first
redraw). Only when nothing is queued behind us does it fall back to training degraded. Cost ~268 s of
setup against 14% of up to 52 min.
- **Applied at BOTH refusal sites in all FOUR launchers**: the blacklist path and the pre-flight path
  share the requeue and therefore shared the bug. The first pass caught only one site per file because
  the two differ by **two spaces of indentation**; a whitespace-tolerant regex found the rest.
  Verified: `2 site(s) covered, 0 unfixed left` in each of the four, all `bash -n` clean,
  `.pre_reqfix`/`.pre_reqfix2` kept.
- The `$10=="H"` successor count was tested against the live queue (`H jobs = 1`) rather than assumed.
- ⚠️ **The current slice is NOT being restarted.** It is 18 min in with ~120 steps done and ~35 min of
  `TRAIN_WALL` left: the remaining penalty is ~5 min of work against ~4.5 min of restart setup plus a
  fresh draw risk. That is break-even, and §M+336's rule: kill a degraded slice only while it has
  produced nothing: says leave it. The fix takes effect at the next boundary.
- ⚠️ Loss read **2.1232** this tick (mean10 1.3833 over only 5 readings) against ~0.9-1.6 earlier. It
  is a resume-adjacent single reading on a 0.0766-sd-per-slice signal (§M+327), so it is noise until a
  full slice mean says otherwise: noted, not acted on.

### §M+342: the §M+341 fix now takes effect at the NEXT boundary instead of the one after, and the line ordering confirms the mechanism. 2026-09-16 19:1x CDT.
`7628716` was submitted by slice 818 at **18:40**, and the §M+341 patch landed at **~18:55**, so its
PBS spool did not carry the fix, and a capped-node draw at the 19:32 boundary would have trained
degraded for another hour. Replaced it: `qdel 7628716`, resubmitted the same launcher with the same
`-W depend=afterany:7628621` → **`7628739`** (H), whose spool does carry the fix. Free, since it was
never running.
**And the ordering that the fix depends on is verified by inspection at the real call site:**
| line | what |
|---|---|
| **278** | `SUCC=$(qsub -m n -W depend=afterany:$PBS_JOBID $SELF_SCRIPT)`, successor created at slice START |
| 293 | `BLFILE=$R/.slow_nodes`: the blacklist check begins |
| 320 | the refusal's own `qsub` (the one that always fails) |
| 336 | the new exit-if-a-successor-is-held branch |
So by the time a slice refuses, **it has already created its own held successor**, which means
`$_succ >= 1` holds and the exit path is live on the FIRST refusal, not only after some later
submission. ⭐ It also closes the loop on *why* the requeue always fails: the slice consumed the
`generic` Q allowance itself, fifteen lines earlier. The failure was self-inflicted by the chain's own
design, which is exactly what §M+341 inferred and this ordering proves.
**Bounded as before:** refuse → exit → successor redraws, at ~175 s of setup per attempt, capped at 3
consecutive refusals by `.preflight_refusals` (whose reset §M+323 made meaningful). Worst case ~9 min
of barren slices instead of ~60 min at −14%. ⚠️ Three barren slices WILL trip `barren_slices`'s
abort-loop alarm: correctly; that is the alarm's purpose, and the text already distinguishes a single
refusal from a run of them.
**Current slice unchanged as decided:** loss **1.3209**, mean10 **1.2409**, the 2.1232 reading last
tick was noise exactly as called, needing no action. Still 12.13 s/step / 44,573 tok/s on the capped

§M+312 parked the standing interconnect task on the premise *"production has no cross-node traffic to
optimise: the trainer is 1 node / 8 GPUs on Sophia, and phase B is the same shape."* **That premise
died at 17:30.** The trainer has been on **Polaris, 2 nodes × 4 A100**, ever since, and may stay for
days (§M+345 prices the remainder at 3.69 days on this shape). The penalty is measured, not assumed:
**Sophia 1-node 7,099 tok/s per GPU vs Polaris 2-node 6,357 → 10.4%**, consistent with the 12.8% and
9.9% on record.
**Audited what production actually exports, since that had never been checked against the record:**
| setting | live launcher | the record |
|---|---|---|
| `aws-ofi-nccl v1.6.0` + `FI_MR_CACHE_MONITOR=memhooks` | ✅ set | the **1.45×** real-training win |
| `NCCL_ALGO` | **`Ring`** | prompt says "Production is now **Tree,Ring**" |
| `NCCL_BUFFSIZE` | **unset** | 32 MB chosen in the microbenchmark |
| `NCCL_PROTO=Simple`, `FI_CXI_*` | set | n/a |
⭐ **The 1.45× production measurement was itself taken with Ring** ("aws-ofi-nccl v1.6.0 + memhooks +
Ring = 49,698 tok/s"), so the launcher matches the number we actually rely on. **`Tree,Ring`'s value in
REAL TRAINING has never been measured**: the 2.31× for Tree is an all-reduce microbenchmark, and the
prompt's own warning is that the benchmark's ordering held while its magnitude did not (predicted
2-3.7×, training gave 1.45×).
⛔ **Not changing it mid-run, deliberately.** `NCCL_ALGO=Tree` alone *crashed* real training twice; a
bad value here does not degrade, it fails, and the successor would inherit the same setting from the
same launcher: a crash loop the 3-strike refusal bound does not cover. The standing task's own rule
("one interconnect job at a time, and only when nothing else of ours is running there") also forbids a
second Polaris job while the trainer holds the debug slot.
⭐ **One open item from the standing prompt IS answered by today's measurement, though:** "HBM headroom
under the REAL training footprint before trying 64 MB". Production HBM is **39.0/42.4 GB = 92.0%**
(§M+337): about 3.4 GB free, and NCCL allocates `BUFFSIZE` **per channel per direction**, so a
32 → 64 MB move is exactly the kind of change that turns a 92% slice into an OOM. **64 MB is ruled out
on this shape**; 32 MB remains untested in training and is the cheaper candidate.
⇒ Revised trigger, replacing §M+312's: run the 2-node interconnect test **when the trainer returns to
Sophia and Polaris is free**, at which point `Tree,Ring` and `BUFFSIZE=32MB` are one A/B each against
a 10.4% penalty that is now a production cost rather than a hypothetical.

### §M+347: phase B's cooldown is now DERIVED from the corpus, closing the `--cooldown` coupling before it can bite a third time. 2026-09-16 20:2x CDT.
`ctx_chain_sn.pbs` carried a literal `--cooldown 1658`, which encodes 15% of 11,053 steps, i.e. it is
correct **only for a 6.0B-token mix**. With `--max_epochs 1` and no `--train_tokens`, **the corpus size
IS the run length** (§M+318), and the mix ratio is still an open decision, so any change to the mix
would silently reshape the WSD schedule: too short a cooldown and the LR never lands, too long and most
of the run is decaying. That is the same family as the `--cooldown 0` bug this project has already hit
**twice, in two different trees** ([[anneal-no-lr-decay-and-general-forgetting]]).
**Fixed by removing the coupling rather than documenting it:** the launcher now computes
`steps = bytes/4/542720` from `$DATA` and sets `COOLDOWN` to 15% of that, overridable with
`COOLDOWN=<n>`, and echoes the derivation into the slice log.
- **Verified the new code reproduces the old value on the old input**: the planned 24.1 GB mix gives
  11,101 steps → **cooldown 1665** against the hardcoded **1658** (0.4%, the difference between
  "24.1 GB" and "exactly 6.0B tokens"). It then tracks correctly off-nominal: an 8B mix → 2,211, a 3B
  mix → 829.
- Fallbacks checked rather than assumed: a missing or unreadable `$DATA` yields `_steps=0`, the
  `-lt 1` guard restores 1658, and the size gate (§M+318) aborts a few lines later anyway. A
  non-numeric override is rejected the same way: **testing the variable, not a defaulted copy**, which
  is the mistake §M+344 made an hour ago.
- Ordering verified at the real call site, because that is what bit twice today: `LOG=` is line 80, the
  derivation line 237, the data aborts 252/257, so the `tee -a $LOG` has a defined target and the
  derivation cannot outrun the guard it depends on.
- `bash -n` clean, md5 `71168afad73f5efe73686ef259e491fe`, `.pre_cooldown` kept. The launcher is
  double-gated and not submitted, so this is free to land now.

### §M+348: I staged a duplicate of an arm that ran two days ago, because I checked the WRONG report directory. Unstaged. 2026-09-16 20:4x CDT.
Pre-registering the three queued cells, I read their configs and found what they actually test:
- **`cdhz4`**, two h800 arms identical but for `cooldown_frac` **0.45 vs 0.60** (same `data_seed=2029`,
  same `seed=622`): a paired cooldown contrast, **n=1 pair**.
- **`dfillseed{588,700,811}`**, three h1600 arms identical but for `seed`: a **run-to-run noise floor**
  at h1600, which is the n≥3 the record keeps asking for ([[muon-lr-closed-at-peak-008]]: "≤0.02
  levers need ≥4 seeds"; the current `run_to_run` floor entry is n=2).
`blockers.sh` listed only 700 and 811, so I concluded 588 was missing from the set and staged it.
**⛔ It was not missing, it RAN on Sep 14 and its result has been sitting in
`/home/youzhi/ArgonneAI/report/n_dfillseed588_h1600_s588.json` ever since.** My check globbed
`exp5/report/`; `blockers.sh` reads `RPT=/home/youzhi/ArgonneAI/report`: the **repo-root** `report/`,
which holds all six `n_dfill*` results. I hand-ran the tool's own loop against the wrong directory,
got 8 unfinished cells against its 3, and trusted my version.
- **Unstaged immediately** (`rm -f` on the explicit path): `/eagle` pending is back to the correct
  **4 arms**. Had it stayed, the next session would have burned ~44 min re-running a finished arm and
  written a second result for the same arm id, which is worse than the wasted time, because a
  duplicated id in a 3-seed floor silently changes the statistic it exists to measure.
- ⭐ **The tool was right and my "fix" was the regression.** Fourth wrong-source-of-truth error today
  (the `tr ","`-before-grep node read, the `qstat -u` truncated id, the `${_pf:-0}` case subject, this).
  The common shape: I reconstructed a check by hand instead of reading the constant the real check
  uses. **When verifying a tool's output, take its inputs from the tool, not from memory of where
  things live.**
⇒ The design needs nothing added: **588 (done) + 700 + 811 (staged) = the 3 seeds**, so the h1600
run-to-run floor lands at n=3 as soon as the session runs. `cdhz4` remains a 2-arm contrast, which at
the probe cell's ≥0.05 resolution ([[probe-cell-power-limit]]) can only support a LARGE cooldown
effect: worth stating before the result exists, not after.

### §M+350: I "fixed" the rate-disagreement message on a wrong sign analysis, broke the file with an apostrophe, and reverted. 2026-09-16 21:1x CDT.
The tick showed `7.50 s/step eff / 10.69 inst ... which is what a checkpoint save looks like`. eff was
**faster** than inst, and I reasoned a save can only make eff *slower*, so the message must be
mislabelling window quantisation. I rewrote it to branch on the sign.
**⛔ The sign analysis was wrong, and the original text was right.** A save produces BOTH directions
depending on where the window falls:
- a window **containing** the save has too few steps ⇒ the delta reads SLOW;
- a window **just after** it has normal steps while tqdm's EMA is still unwinding ⇒ the delta reads
  FAST against an inflated instantaneous figure. That is this case exactly (a save landed at 210842 and
  the EMA was still recovering).
The existing wording: *"save stalls the delta, EMA stalls tqdm; steady state is neither"*, already
names both mechanisms. **Reverted in full**; `bash -n` clean and the line reads normally again
(`10.65 s/step / 50,767 tok/s`), with `blockers.sh` at 0 NEEDS ATTENTION and no shell errors.
- ⛔ **And the edit broke the script outright**: my explanatory comment sat inside the awk program,
  which is **single-quoted in the shell**, and it contained an apostrophe (`tqdm's`) plus backticks.
  `bash -n` reported `unexpected EOF while looking for matching '`. `trainer_status.sh` is called by
  `blockers.sh` every tick, so a broken file here blinds the tick: caught only because I ran `bash -n`
  in the same command as the edit. **This is the apostrophe-inside-a-quoted-block trap already on the
  record** (`python -c '...'`), and the third quoting-in-an-embedded-program failure today after the
  two backtick-in-an-ssh-payload ones.
⭐ **The rule those three share, now stated once:** an embedded program (awk in single quotes, a shell
payload in double quotes, python in `-c`) is not a place for prose. Comments about it go OUTSIDE the
quotes, in the host script. I have now broken this three times in one day while writing the comment
that explains the previous break.
⚠️ **And the analysis error is the more expensive half:** I was about to make a monitor *less* accurate
in the name of precision, on a line I read every 15 minutes. The check that caught it was enumerating
what a save does to each clock in each window position, i.e. working the mechanism, not the sign.

### §M+351: the wall-save reserve checked at the wall: ~208 s used of 450 s, and the two save figures measure different things. 2026-09-16 21:2x CDT.
Caught slice 822 mid-wall-save and followed it to the end rather than inferring:
`POLARIS slice 822 … Thu Sep 17 01:32:14 AM UTC` + `TRAIN_WALL=3150` ⇒ training stops **02:24:44 UTC**;
`Approaching wall limit … Saving checkpoint and exiting` was already printed at 02:27:50, and by
**02:28:12** the log read `[retention] checkpoint at step 211112 verified; pruning older checkpoints`
with `checkpoint_step_210842.pt` removed (23.1 GiB freed). So the **whole wall-save: write, md5
verify, prune: took ≤208 s** against the **450 s** the guard reserves (`TRAIN_WALL = 3600 − 450`),
leaving ~240 s of headroom on a 1 h slice. The reserve is correctly sized; its commit message asked
for measurement instead of inheritance, and this is that measurement taken at the wall rather than in
the middle of a slice.
⭐ **And it reconciles two numbers that look contradictory:** §M+322 measured **84 s** per save from the
tqdm elapsed-clock gaps, and that is right, it is the **in-loop stall only**. The wall-save
additionally md5-verifies and prunes *after* the loop exits, which tqdm cannot see. **84 s is the
throughput cost; ~200 s is the wall-clock cost.** Quoting either for the other is the mistake, and the
reserve must be sized against the second.
- Step 211112 is on /eagle and the mirror picks it up on its next 15-min tick; the successor resumes
  from it, so the boundary again cost no work.
- Trainer at the time: loss **1.0490**, mean10 1.2445, 10.65 s/step / 50,767 tok/s / 6,345 per GPU,
  HBM 92.0%, 0 NEEDS ATTENTION.

`nccl_train6.pbs:129`, in its own words: *"round 2 showed **NCCL_BUFFSIZE (pure bandwidth) is a null in
training** because the all-reduce is already hidden, so CROSS_NIC, also a bandwidth lever: is
predicted null by the same argument."*
- ⛔ **§M+346 called `BUFFSIZE=32MB` "the cheaper untested candidate". That is wrong and is retracted.**
  It is tested and null. The microbenchmark's 8.62 GB/s at 32 MB is real and irrelevant: the all-reduce
  overlaps backward compute, so only the *unhidden tail* is exposed, which is why the benchmark

  while the collective stays hidden. That is what let the harness drop CROSS_NIC without testing it: 
  a prediction, recorded as such. `NCCL_ALGO=Tree,Ring` is NOT covered, because Tree changes the
  algorithm's latency structure rather than its bandwidth.

  training twice**, so it belongs in the harness (which runs arms in an isolated dir with its own
  wall) and not in the production launcher, and the harness's round 5 was already decomposing the
  residual penalty (arm E 2-node-2gpu cross-node vs arm F 1-node-4gpu reference at matched
  micro-steps), which is the open question the prompt phrases as "it may not be NCCL at all".

arm, §M+349 re-derived floors, §M+350 wrong sign, this). They share one cheap remedy I keep skipping:

doubling an assumed h400 ≈ 11 min taken from the standing prompt's *4-arm session* arithmetic, instead
of dividing the arm's own token count by a measured rate. **A horizon is tokens; a wall is seconds; the

### §M+362: "3 refusals IN A ROW" was not in a row: the strike count survived 162 minutes of Sophia training. Given a TTL. 2026-09-17 00:1x CDT.
`$R/.preflight_refusals` read **1**, set at **21:30 CDT**, the Polaris slice that refused a blacklisted
node just before Sophia took the node back, and it was still 1 **162 minutes later**. §M+323 made a
clean node draw reset it, which is right, but if Polaris stops being the trainer *no draw happens* and
the count simply persists. So the next Polaris episode (01:12 at the earliest) would have started with
a strike already banked, and two refusals would have tipped it into "train degraded on a capped node".
That is not "in a row" in any useful sense: the bound would have spanned two unrelated episodes hours
apart.
**Fixed in all four Polaris launchers, at both `PFSTRIKE=` sites each (8 edits):** a counter older than
`STRIKE_TTL_MIN=180` is cleared, with a log line naming the value it discarded.
- **The TTL is arithmetic, not taste:** a real abort loop iterates every ~3 min (175 s setup + refuse +
  exit), so three iterations take **~9 min**. 180 min is **20×** that, it cannot interfere with a
  genuine loop, and it guarantees a fresh episode starts clean. The three numbers are in the comment so
  the next person to tighten it argues with data.
- Both directions tested on `/tmp` fixtures rather than the live file: a 0-min counter is **kept**, a
  200-min counter is **EXPIRED**. And the live one (162 min, value 1) is correctly **kept**, it is
  under the TTL, so the fix is not silently erasing current state.
- `bash -n` clean on all four; `.pre_ttl` copies kept. Reaches the next submission, which is the parked
  insurance's successor.

### §M+363: I nearly reported a phase-A loss trend off five falling `mean10` values. They are a rolling window, and the raw sd is 0.333. 2026-09-17 00:2x CDT.
`mean10` fell on five consecutive ticks: **1.2894 → 1.1576 → 1.0969 → 0.9866 → 0.9257**, which looks
like the first sign of movement in phase A. Tested it instead of reporting it, on the 24 raw
`Step N | Loss` readings behind those means (steps 211,940-212,170):
| | |
|---|---|
| per-reading sd | **0.3330** (range **1.2079**, min 0.640, max 1.848) |
| first 12 vs last 12 | 1.1374 → 0.9614, **delta −0.1759** |
| se of that difference | 0.1359 ⇒ **t = 1.29, NOT significant** |
⛔ **And the five-fall "run" carries far less weight than it appears:** `mean10` averages ten
**overlapping** readings, so consecutive values share 9 of 10 samples and are ~0.9 correlated. One low
reading entering the window drags several successive means down. **Five falls are worth roughly one
observation**, not five: the same shape as the retracted "3-point CE trend" the record already warns
about, arriving through a smoothed statistic instead of a raw one.
⭐ **The rule this fixes, stated with its numbers:** gate any phase-A loss claim on **slice means**
(sd **0.0766**, ~170 readings each, §M+327): never on `mean10` (autocorrelated) and never on raw
readings (sd **0.333**, i.e. **4.3×** the slice-level noise). At the slice level the smallest resolvable
move is ~0.088; at the raw level a 0.18 swing is inside one standard error.

LR is flat at 2e-4 and `--cooldown 5012` does not begin until local step 28,402 (we are at 8,709).

one's tell**: the observable that identifies it before the verdict is trusted (`command not found`
for a tool you never invoked; a filename with a flag glued to its front; a duration that is a round
multiple of a tick; a count that disagrees with the tool's by a large factor). INFRA sections nobody
greps are the wrong home for a recurring failure mode; a memory is the right one.
**And the two rules that would have caught all nine, stated once:**
1. **An embedded program is not a place for prose**: awk in single quotes, a shell payload in double
   quotes, python in `-c`. Comments go outside the quotes. I broke this three times today, each time
   while writing the comment explaining the previous break.
2. **When verifying a tool, take its inputs FROM the tool**, its constants, its directory, its own
   logged start/end, not from memory of where things live. And attach the filter to the wide command
   rather than after it: one unfiltered `pbsnodes` printed 256 CPU-slot entries to answer "which job
   holds this node".

different shapes** (Sophia 1 node × 8 GPU, Polaris 2 nodes × 4+4), so if the loss *level* differed by
host, every pooled trend estimate would be contaminated by which host happened to hold the node.
Measured from logs already on disk, per-slice mean loss for every phase-A slice with ≥25 readings:

|---|---|---|---|

host term to carry. That is the expected answer: the global batch and the data order are keyed to the
global step, so DDP should be shape-invariant, but "expected" is not "checked", and this was free.

(2 se), which is essentially identical to the slice-level resolution floor of **0.088** from §M+327. So

cannot be ruled out, and also cannot influence any decision taken with that statistic.

### §M+374: phase A's HF export had NO offsite backup: the script written because an export "would exist in ONE place" was hardcoded to the previous one. 2026-09-17 03:4x CDT.
Forward-looking check with ~2.7-3.7 days of lead time, on the artifact phase A produces at the end.
`anneal_chain_sn.pbs` passes `--final_model_dir $R/ckpt/anneal_model_complete` and
`--completion_marker $R/.continue_pretrain_complete`. `final_export_backup.sh` was hardcoded to
`SRC=$R/ckpt/final_model_complete` and gated on `[ -f $R/.pretrain_complete ]`: **the pretrain's
export**. So when phase A finishes, its publishable HF model would have lived on **/eagle alone**,
which is the exact failure this script's own header exists to prevent, one stage later. Same shape as
`eagle_mirror_tick.sh` needing `CKSUB`/`DSUB` for the anneal checkpoints (§M+317).
**Fixed by parameterising, defaults reproducing today's behaviour, plus a second crontab line:**
| | pretrain (default) | anneal (new line) |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPORT_SUB` | `final_model_complete` | `anneal_model_complete` |
| `EXPORT_MARK` | `.pretrain_complete` | `.continue_pretrain_complete` |
| `DST` | `…/argonne45_pretrain/final_model_complete` | `…/argonne45_pretrain/anneal_model_complete` |
| `LOG` | `final_export_backup.log` (**unchanged**) | `final_export_backup_anneal.log` |
Both invocations traced with `bash -x` to confirm the paths, and both run clean now (the markers are
absent, so each exits 0 silently: the correct pre-completion state). `crontab -l | grep -c
final_export_backup.sh` → **2**.
- ⚠️ **My first version broke the consumer it was meant to leave alone:** I derived the log name from
  `$EXPORT_SUB`, which silently renamed the live log to `final_export_backup_final_model_complete.log`.
  The tag is now a separate variable defaulting to **empty**, so the pretrain run keeps writing the
  file it has always written. *A parameterisation that renames an existing artifact is not
  backward-compatible, however sensible the new name looks.*
- The gate stays on the **marker**, not on the directory, for the reason already in the header: the
  export is written file-by-file, so a directory that exists may be half-written.

### §M+376: the numerical liveness check was never automated: it ran once, by hand, in September. Now it fires on the verified copy. 2026-09-17 04:1x CDT.
Continuing the §M+374/375 sweep: *who else is pinned to the finished stage, or to me remembering?*, 
I grepped every `~/bin` script and /eagle launcher for `pretrain_complete`/`final_model_complete` (12
and 30 hits) and triaged to the ones that take an ACTION rather than report. `export_liveness.sh` was
the standout, and it is the sibling of the gap I closed two ticks ago.
**It is NOT stage-pinned**, it takes the export dir as `$1` with a default, so it always could have
checked the anneal export. **The problem is that nothing calls it**: `crontab -l | grep
export_liveness` → nothing; `grep export_liveness final_export_backup.sh` → nothing. The pretrain
export carries a `.liveness` record dated **Sep 14 12:26** because I ran it by hand. For the phase-A
export that meant a **backed-up, md5-verified, never-numerically-checked** artifact: the one that
becomes phase B's input and eventually the published model, with *"someone remembers"* as the
mechanism.
⭐ **Why this check is not redundant with md5:** the script's own header says it, 338 tensors, index
and headers agreeing, no offsets past EOF, vocab trimmed in the weights as well as the config, md5
identical on both ends: **not one of those touches the numbers.** A truncated or randomly-initialised
tensor file passes every structural test. The first forward pass is the first evidence the weights are
a trained model, and it costs ~3 s on CPU.
**Wired into `final_export_backup.sh` at the verified-copy point**, which is the correct trigger: the
bytes are known complete exactly there. Three safeguards, each for a failure already on the record:
- **gated on `.liveness` absence** ⇒ runs once per export, not every 15 min (the pretrain's existing
  record dated Sep 14 confirms it will not re-run);
- **its failure cannot change the backup verdict**: logged as a ⚠️, never propagated (§M+333: a
  diagnostic must not be able to break what it inspects);
- **writing another dotfile into `$DST` is safe only because** the manifest comparison excludes
  dotfiles **by class** on both sides (`-not -name '.*'`, lines 92-94). That exclusion began as a
  one-filename fix that *this very sentinel* broke; checked before adding to it.

### §M+380: ⛔ I wrote a burn-rate conclusion BEFORE running the arithmetic, and then differenced the wrong column. Corrected. 2026-09-17 05:1x CDT.
The check was worth doing: the standing prompt's walltime prudence exists because of depletion emails
and Polaris has now carried the run ~11.7 h, but I made two errors in one section and both are worth
recording.
**Error 1: I drafted the numbers before computing them.** The first version of this entry asserted
"2.41 node-h per wall hour, 1.21× overlap, 211 node-hours, 543 days": values I had not run. The
calculation then printed 8.50 / 4.25× / 743 / 154. **Writing a conclusion and then checking it is not
the same as checking and then writing**, and a plausible number in a record is worse than none.
**Error 2, the substantive one: `Available Balance` is not `start − charged`.** Two readings:
| when | Jobs | Charged | Available Balance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-16 21:55 | 1,282 | 2,012.0 | 31,481.9 |
| 2026-09-17 05:12 | 1,288 | 2,018.2 | 31,420.3 |
**Charged rose 6.2 node-hours while Available Balance fell 61.6**: the two columns disagree by 10×,
so differencing the balance measures something other than consumption (most plausibly a hold against
queued jobs, which we have four of on Sophia and two on Polaris). ⭐ **`Charged` is the consumption
column.**
**Charged +6.2 node-h over 7.25 h**, and that reconciles with the shape: Polaris trained
01:33→05:12 = 3.65 h × 2 nodes = **7.3 node-h**, plus ~0.5 for the experiment session and ~0.5 for the
wake-and-yield cycles, against a window in which Sophia (a *different* allocation) held the run from
21:30 to 01:22. So the real rate while Polaris trains is ~2 node-h/h as expected, and the 8.50 figure
was an artefact of the wrong column.

remaining ~87 h on Polaris costs **~175 node-hours on `Charged`** (or 743 on the pessimistic balance
reading) against **31,420 available**: **0.6%**, or 2.4% at worst. The prudence directive is satisfied
